primary_diagnosis_treated: Advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD stage 5) secondary to diabetic and hypertensive nephropathy

medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after any dose change (creatinine & potassium at 1–2 weeks)
medications.purpose: Renal protection and blood pressure control for CKD with proteinuria
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line ACE inhibitor for CKD with ACR ≥30 mg/mmol or hypertension; monitor creatinine and potassium after 1–2 weeks

medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after any change in renal function
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends BP target <140/90 mmHg (or <130/80 mmHg if ACR ≥70 mg/mmol); thiazide can be used as part of regimen
Guideline does not prohibit CCB use; included for rhythm control

medications.dose: 5 mg orally once daily (dose adjusted to INR 2‑3)
medications.purpose: Stroke prophylaxis in atrial fibrillation with high thrombo‑embolic risk
medications.nice_justification: Anticoagulation required for AF; not a CKD‑specific recommendation but essential

medications.duration: Lifelong — monitor serum digoxin level and renal function
medications.nice_justification: Standard therapy for AF; compatible with CKD when dose adjusted

medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and titrate to 40 mg if LDL‑C target not met
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a risk‑equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203: Statin for all CKD patients for CV risk reduction

medications.dose: 650 mg orally three times daily (adjust to maintain serum HCO₃⁻ ≥22 mmol/L)
medications.duration: Until serum bicarbonate ≥22 mmol/L, then review every 3 months
medications.purpose: Correct metabolic acidosis secondary to advanced CKD
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends oral bicarbonate when HCO₃⁻ <22 mmol/L

medications.dose: 50,000 IU subcutaneously once weekly (dose titrated to Hb 10‑11 g/dL)
medications.duration: Until Hb 10‑11 g/dL, then review every 3 months
medications.purpose: Treat CKD‑related anaemia when Hb <10 g/dL and iron stores repleted
medications.nice_justification: NG203 anaemia screening; ESA indicated when Hb <10 g/dL after iron repletion

medications.dose: 200 mg orally once daily (taken ≥2 h apart from other meds)
medications.duration: Until ferritin >100 µg/L or transferrin saturation >20 %, then review
medications.purpose: Correct iron deficiency to optimise response to ESA
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends iron supplementation before ESA therapy in CKD anaemia

medications.dose: 145 mg orally once daily (dose reduced for eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m²)
medications.duration: Lifelong — monitor renal function, CK and liver enzymes every 3 months
medications.nice_justification: CKD dyslipidaemia management; dose adjustment per renal function (NG203 non‑pharmacological guidance)

interactions_checked.interaction: Statins can potentiate warfarin anticoagulant effect, leading to increased INR and bleeding risk
interactions_checked.action: Check INR 2–3 days after starting atorvastatin, then weekly for 2 weeks; adjust warfarin dose as needed

interactions_checked.interaction: Verapamil inhibits CYP3A4, increasing atorvastatin plasma concentrations and risk of myopathy
interactions_checked.action: Use standard atorvastatin dose (20 mg) with close monitoring for muscle symptoms; consider CK measurement if symptoms develop

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined use increases risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis; fenofibrate may also raise serum creatinine
interactions_checked.action: Monitor CK and renal function every 3 months; advise patient to report muscle pain promptly

interactions_checked.interaction: Verapamil can increase digoxin levels, raising toxicity risk
interactions_checked.action: Check serum digoxin level after initiating/verifying verapamil dose; adjust digoxin if needed

contraindications.reason: eGFR 9.5 mL/min/1.73 m² (CKD stage 5) – NSAIDs accelerate CKD progression and cause fluid retention
contraindications.alternative: Paracetamol for analgesia; consider topical agents if needed

contraindications.reason: eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² – high risk of lactic acidosis
Guideline contraindicates dual RAAS blockade due to hyperkalaemia and AKI risk
contraindications.alternative: Continue ACE‑I alone (lisinopril) as per guideline

contraindications.reason: eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² – high risk of contrast‑induced nephropathy
contraindications.alternative: Use low‑osmolar contrast with prophylactic hydration and N‑acetylcysteine if imaging unavoidable

assumptions_warnings: Serum potassium not provided – baseline K⁺ required before any ACE‑I dose change and to monitor for hyperkalaemia.
Liver function tests not provided – baseline ALT/AST needed before initiating atorvastatin.
Full lipid profile (LDL‑C, total cholesterol) not available – required to confirm need for statin titration.
Hemoglobin, ferritin and transferrin saturation not provided – needed to confirm indication for ESA and iron supplementation.
Current blood pressure reading not provided – required to assess adequacy of antihypertensive regimen.
Allergy status unknown – verify no hypersensitivity to ACE‑I, statin, bicarbonate, iron or ESA.
treatment_summary: The plan continues ACE‑I therapy for renal protection, adds a statin for cardiovascular risk reduction, corrects metabolic acidosis with sodium bicarbonate, and addresses CKD‑related anaemia with ESA and iron once labs confirm need. Hypertriglyceridaemia is managed with low‑dose fenofibrate, with careful monitoring for myopathy. All new drugs are compatible with the existing regimen except for a moderate interaction between atorvastatin and warfarin, which requires INR monitoring. NSAIDs, metformin and dual ACE‑I/ARB therapy are contraindicated in this patient with eGFR 9.5 mL/min/1.73 m².
